sentences.text: The genus Unquillosaurus contains only one species, U. ceibalii, known solely from a single fossilized pubis bone.
This dinosaur is estimated to have reached 3 meters in length, 1.40 meters in height, and weighed nearly 40 kilograms.
The holotype specimen PVL 3670-11 was discovered at Arroyo-Morterito in the Los Blanquitos Formation dating to the Maastrichtian.
The type species Unquillosaurus ceibalii was described by Jaime Eduardo Powell in 1979.

Powell originally assigned Unquillosaurus to the Carnosauria in 1979. In 2004, Novas and Agnolin concluded that Unquillosaurus belonged to Maniraptora or at least Maniraptoriformes based on opisthopubic pelvic anatomy. In 2006, Martínez and Novas suggested that Unquillosaurus likely belonged to the maniraptoran clade Dromaeosauridae. In 2012, Carrano and colleagues classified Unquillosaurus as a member of Carcharodontosauridae due to similarities with Giganotosaurus. In 2024, researchers considering the taxonomy of Diuqin suggested Unquillosaurus might be a member of the Unenlagiinae. The Paleobiology Database lists the parent group of Unquillosaurus as Carcharodontosauridae.
